daily_brief: Sunday's news is dominated by escalating military actions across multiple theaters. Ukraine launched what Moscow's mayor called an 'unprecedented' drone attack on the Russian capital, with 450 drones intercepted and at least two civilians killed, while an oil refinery was damaged [BBC, ABC Australia, Le Monde]. The attack coincides with the final day of Russia's first wartime parliamentary election. In the Middle East, Houthi militants struck the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles for the first time since escalating hostilities in July, prompting US travel warnings [BBC, France 24, Financial Times, Al Jazeera]. Diplomatically, the US and Denmark announced a security agreement over Greenland, resolving months of tension sparked by President Trump's annexation threats, with NATO welcoming the deal [BBC, The Economist, France 24]. In Germany, state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern could deliver another blow to Chancellor Merz's CDU following the far-right AfD's recent gains [BBC, Financial Times, Le Monde]. Meanwhile, French President Macron warned of intensifying Russian hybrid attacks against Europe and ordered enhanced protection of critical infrastructure [BBC].

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Launches 'Unprecedented' Drone Attack on Moscow, Killing Two
bullets: Moscow Mayor Sobyanin reported 450 drones were shot down en route to the capital in what he called an 'unprecedented attack'; Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 1,100 Ukrainian drones were intercepted nationwide
At least two civilians were killed and six injured in the Moscow region; an oil refinery was damaged and several homes set ablaze
Ukraine's President Zelensky confirmed strikes hit a 'key' Russian oil facility and logistics site, calling them targets worth 'billions of dollars that sustain the war machine'
The attack coincides with the final day of Russia's first parliamentary election since the 2022 invasion, which the Kremlin has framed as a test of public support for the war

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage presenting both Russian casualty claims and Ukrainian strategic justification

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized scale of attack and election timing context

top_stories.headline: Houthi Missiles Strike Saudi Capital Riyadh in Major Escalation
bullets: Iran-backed Houthi militants launched ballistic missiles and drones at Riyadh, with Saudi authorities confirming interception of at least one missile; air raid alerts sounded in the capital for the first time since July
Black smoke was seen rising from fuel tanks near Riyadh's international airport, causing temporary flight disruptions
Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting additional attacks targeting the cities of Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu
The US State Department urged Americans to 'seriously reconsider travel to and through the region' citing potential for rapid escalation

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Factual reporting with emphasis on US travel warning

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief coverage noting this as first strike on Riyadh

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Included expert analysis predicting 'sizeable Saudi response'

top_stories.headline: US and Denmark Reach Greenland Security Deal After Months of Trump Threats
bullets: The US and Denmark announced a security agreement granting the US 'permanent control over security' in Greenland, according to President Trump, though no official text has been released
The deal reportedly prohibits any US adversary from maintaining military presence or making sensitive investments in Greenland without US approval
NATO welcomed the agreement as helping 'advance security, stability and cooperation' in the Arctic region
The deal resolves diplomatic tensions sparked by Trump's repeated threats to 'take' Greenland by force, citing its strategic location and mineral wealth

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage noting deal terms remain unclear

sources.name: The Economist
sources.framing_note: Critical framing noting annexation threats caused lasting diplomatic damage despite deal

top_stories.headline: German State Elections Threaten Fresh Blow to Chancellor Merz
bullets: Voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern are casting ballots in state elections where polls suggest Chancellor Merz's CDU faces potential defeats
In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the CDU is polling near the 5% threshold required to enter the state parliament, risking their worst-ever state election result
The elections follow the far-right AfD's major victory in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago, where the CDU's vote was halved
Speculation is mounting about a potential mid-term replacement of Merz unless CDU fortunes improve, though potential challengers remain hesitant

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive coverage of political stakes for Merz

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Article unavailable but headline confirmed coverage; separate opinion piece analyzed German democratic systems fueling extremism

top_stories.headline: Macron Warns of Intensifying Russian Hybrid Attacks Against Europe
bullets: French President Macron declared that Russian hybrid attacks against Europe and France have intensified in recent weeks
Macron ordered a plan to protect critical infrastructure and defense industry sites in response to the threat
The president cited last month's drone attack on Leipzig airport in Germany and Polish PM Tusk's warnings of potential Russian strikes against NATO's eastern flank
Macron stated France has been targeted by Russian hybrid attacks recently and they would not be left 'without a response'

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting of Macron's statements and broader European context
